subject: Mathematics
title: Friends in Shelf
subtitle: Counting in tens up to 100
hero_picture: A bright school library with tall wooden shelves full of colourful books, a smiling teacher with glasses and Kerala school children choosing books.

sections.heading: Bundles of ten
text: Malu got many books on her birthday.
She tied them in bundles of 10.
sections.caption: Two bundles of ten books
sections.picture: A girl at a table with two neat bundles of 10 books each, tied with string, in a classroom.

sections.heading: Books on the shelf
text: Each row on the shelf has ten books.
sections.caption: Ten books in each row
sections.picture: A bookshelf with 5 rows, each row holding exactly 10 colourful books, a boy and a girl counting them.

sections.heading: Mango baskets
text: Nanu Chettan had 50 mangoes in a basket.
The children added 10 more each time: 60, 70, 80, 90.
sections.caption: Filling the mango baskets
sections.picture: A mango grove: an old farmer with a basket of mangoes and children each putting mangoes into baskets, 10 mangoes in each basket.

sections.heading: Threading beads
text: Malu threaded 20 yellow beads and 3 red beads.
sections.caption: A bead necklace
sections.picture: Two girls threading beads at a table: a necklace with 20 yellow beads and a few red beads.

sections.heading: Numbers up to 100
text: Let us play snakes and ladders.
Write 1 to 100 in order on the board.
sections.caption: Snakes and ladders
sections.picture: Children playing a snakes-and-ladders board game on the floor, with a dice; the board squares are plain with no numbers written.

activity: Collect 30 small sticks. Make bundles of ten and count: ten, twenty, thirty.
talk: How many books are in one bundle?
summary: We can count in tens: 10, 20, 30 ... 100; and 20 and 3 make 23.

questions.explanation: Two bundles of ten make twenty.

questions.prompt: 5 rows with 10 books each. How many books?
